8209.html:
8209 píbati 'drinks' RV. [√pā¹]
    Pa. pibati, pivati (pipa- in imper. pipa and pres. part. pipaṁ is prob. hyper-paliism for piva- or due to pipāsā-, &c.), NiDoc. pivaṁti 3 pl., Pk. pibaï, pi(v)aï, Gy. eur. pĭ̄-, arm. pi-, pal. pī-, Ḍ. pīna, Ash. pĭ̄-, Wg. Kt. pī-, Pr. wī-, Dm. pi-, Tir. Paš.pī-, Niṅg. Shum. pi-, Woṭ. pō- (pres. pōn, f. pyēn < *pivantō, °tī), Gaw. Kal. Kho. pi-, Bshk. Tor. pū- (< *piu- AO xviii 246), Phal. pī-, Sh.gil. pióĭki̯, koh. gur. pyōnṷ, K. (Lallā) piwun (cyonu 'to drink', caus. cyāwun with c < py??), S. piaṇu, L. pīvaṇ, P. pīṇā, WPah.bhad. bhal. pāḍ. paṅ. bhiḍ. pī-, cur. pe-, Ku. piṇo, N. piunu, A. piba, B. piyā, Or. piibā, Mth. piab, Bhoj. piyal, OAw. piaï, H. pīnā, OG. pīi, G. pīvũ, M. piṇẽ, Ko. pittā 3 sg. pres., Si. bonavā, pret. bīvā, pīma sb. 'drink, drinking'. — Pa. pivana- n. 'drinking'; Pk. pi(v)aṇa- n. 'drinking, milk'; Ku. piṇo 'mother's milk'; M. pīṇ f. 'sucking of the breasts'. — See Add.
    Addenda: píbati: S.kcch. pīṇū 'to drink', caus. pyārṇū 'to irrigate (a field)'; WPah.kṭg. (kc.) pīṇõ 'to drink', Garh. peṇu, caus. pilɔṇu; Md. bonī 'drinks' (absol. boi, boyi, bō; buim 'I drank, the act of drinking'), bovanī 'is thirsty'; bovenī 'gets drunk up'.

2245.html:
2245 úpaviśati 'approaches' RV., 'sits down' ŚBr. — Pp. upaviṣṭa- 'seated' KātyŚr., °aka- 'remaining too long in the womb' Car. 2. upavēśayati 'causes to sit' AitBr. [√viś]
    Many forms present phonetic difficulty. Initial b-, in all lggs. except Gypsy (arm. as. pal.) and Sindhi, is poss. < early MIA. *uba- which, despite v- in arm. and pal. Gypsy, is more likely than later spread of b- forms from the East (where v- > b-). Contamination with vásati which by itself provides a verb 'to sit' in N. A. B. Or. Again nearly all, whether X vásati or not, have past stem or a new pres. stem from upaviṣṭa-.
    1. Pa. upavisati 'approaches', aor. upāvisi 'sat down'; Pk. uvavisaï, bēsaē 'sits': uvaviṭṭha-, biṭṭha-; Ap. baïsaï: baïṭṭha-; Gy. pal. wḗsăr 'stops, stays, sits': imper. wḗšti (founded on pp., cf. imper. ār 'come!' < ā́gata-), arm. ves- 'to sit', eur. beš-: boh. bešto 'lying', eng. bešto 'saddle'; Ḍ. bēšina 'to sit down': bēṭa; Kaṭ. baiṭhe 'we are sitting'; Tir. bēz- (z < -s-); baxta 'sitting' (X *vasta-); Bshk. bäy-: bāeṣṭ; Tor. baiyūsa (imper. bⁱhai): bēṭh, bēḍū; Phal. bhεš-, bhaš-: bhεṭ, bhaṭ; Sh. gil. băyóĭki̯ 'to sit, dwell' (< vásati?): bε῀ṭu, gur. koh. byōnṷ: bēṭu; K. bĕhun, bih°: byūṭhᵘ (beṭh m. 'sitting, delay'), kash. bihunᵘ; S. vehaṇu, vih°: veṭho; L. bêhaṇ, pres. part. bāhndā: beiṭhā, awāṇ. bâuṇ; P. baiṭhṇā, vaiṭhvā̃, bai° 'in a sitting position', bhaṭ. baiṭhĕā; WPah. cam. baihṇā, paṅ. biśuṇā, pāḍ. bēśaṇ: biṭṭhā, cur. bĕśṇū: bĕṭhā, roh. bašṇõ, boṭhṇõ, bhad. biśṇō, bhal. biśṇū (pp. biśśo); Ku. baiṭhaṇo 'to sit'; B. baisā, basā (< bais- ? or vásati?), dial. baiṭhā (ODBL 513); Or. baïṭhibā, baïṭhā; OMth. baisaï: Mth. baiṭhab; Bhoj. baisal, baiṭhal; OAw. baïsāī 'she was made to sit', baïṭhaï; H. baisnā: baiṭhā, baiṭhnā; OMarw. baïsāi caus.: baïthā, baiṭhaï; G. bεsvũ: bεṭho; M. baisṇẽ, bas°; Ko. baistā, bas°.
    2. Phal. bhεšū́- 'to make sit down'.
    upaviṣṭa- see prec.
    Addenda: úpaviśati (see also vásati). 1. WPah.kṭg. béśṇõ (pret. béśśɔ) 'to sit' (-e- X upavēśá-, etc. Him.I 140), caus. kṭg. (Wkc.) bəśέḷnõ 'to seat', OMarw. (Vīsaḷa) baïsāryaü caus. pret. 'made sit'.
    2. upaviṣṭa-: WPah.poet. bεṭhṇa 'to sit down' (← H.? Him.I 137), J. beṭhṇu, Garh. bεṭhṇu.
    upaviṣṭa- see úpaviśati Add².

6141.html:
6141 dádāti 'gives' RV. [√dā¹]
    Pa. dadāti 'gives'; EAś. fut. dāhaṁti < dāsyánti; NiDoc. dadāti, ger. dadavo, Paš.lauṛ. day- IIFL iii 3, 62; Kal. 2 sg. imper. deh < dēhí; Kho. 3 sg. imper. diyār < dádātu, 2 sg. det < daddhí; Bshk. da-, 1st sg. pres. ya dānt (< pres. part. dádat-, Pa. dadantō); Mai. 1 sg. dam, imper. dē, Phal. dūm, deh, Sh.chil. deh, K. dih.
    Pres. st. dā́ti RV. (> Pk. dāi) was replaced by dēti ~ pp. *dita- after nēti < náyati (for interaction of verbs 'give' and 'take' see P. Tedesco JAOS 43, 364 ff.) and further influenced by 2 sg. imper. dēhí: Pa. dēti, NiDoc. dedi (denati after giṁnati < gr̥hṇā́ti Burrow KharDoc 44), Pk. dēi, Gy. 3 sg. del, pal. der, arm le-, Ḍ. dena, Pr. ā-lye-, Tir. 1 sg. dēm, Paš. weg. chil. Woṭ. dē-, Kal.rumb. dem (pret. pra < prā́dāt), Tor. de-, Sh. dem; K. dyunᵘ, rām. dēṇu, pog. deun, kash. dyunŭ, ḍoḍ. dēṇo, S. ḍ̠iaṇu, pres. part. ḍ̠ī˜do, L. devaṇ, ḍe°, (Ju.) ḍ̠e°, awāṇ. deuṇ, P. deṇā, WPah. all dial. dē-, Ku. diṇo, N. dinu, A. diba, B. deoyā, Or. debā, Mth. deb, Bhoj. 3 sg. fut. dihī, OAw. dei, H. denā, Marw. deṇo, G. devũ, M. deṇẽ, Si. denavā. — See dattá-.
    Addenda: dádāti: S.kcch. ḍeṇū 'to give', WPah.kṭg. dε῀ṇõ (pret. dinnɔ see dattá-), Wkc. dεṇno (pres. dεa, pres.part. dεndo, ṇ of inf. from past dεṇo < *dina- see dattá-), kc. deṇo, J. deṇu; kṭg. caus. dəlauṇõ (← H. dilānā), Garh. deṇu, caus. dilɔṇu; Md. denī 'gives' (inf. dēn, absol. dī, 3 sg.pres. dē; pp. din see dattá-), devanī 'gives in marriage', devenī 'is given'.

7027.html:
7027 náśyati 'is lost, perishes, runs away' RV. 2. Pp. naṣṭá- RV. [√naś¹]
    1. Pa. nassati, NiDoc. naśyati, naśati; Pk. ṇassaï, ṇāsaï 'perishes, runs away'; Gy. eur. naš- 'to run away, go away', arm. nasu- 'to run away, be lost'; Ḍ. nΛš- 'to be lost'; Shum. nas- 'to flow (of tears, water, &c.)'; Woṭ. naš- 'to become bad (of milk)', našel 'bad (of milk)'; Kal.rumb. nāš- 'to die'; Sh.gil. našóĭki̯ 'to be lost', koh. nŏšōnṷ, gur. năšōnṷ; K. naśun 'to be destroyed, disappear', ḍoḍ. naśṇo 'to run'; L. nassaṇ 'to flee', awāṇ. nasuṇ, P. nassṇā, bhaṭ. nhasṇā; WPah.bhaḍ. naśṇū 'to run', bhiḍ. naśśu pp. n. sg., paṅ. cur. naśṇā; Ku. nāsṇo 'to perish, leave, go' (whence nasṇo to distinguish from tr.); Or. nasibā 'to be destroyed, shrink back in fear' (with a from caus. nasāibā); OAw. nāsaï 'perishes'; H. nā̆snā 'to be lost, escape, flee'; G. nāsvũ 'to flee'; M. nāsṇẽ 'to be spoilt'; Ko. nāstā 'curdles (of milk)'; Si. nasinavā, nahi° 'to die'.
    2. Forms pp. and pret. to present stems from náśyati: Pa. naṭṭha-, Pk. ṇaṭṭha-; Gy. eur. našto 'gone away', pal. năšt- 'to flee'; Ḍ. nΛtha (= -ṭh- ?); Dm. naṣṭo 'he died' (pret. of br- < mriyátē), Kal. nāšta NTS xii 160, rumb. naṣṭa-ǰīre 'burial feast'; Sh. naṭŭ; K. nūṭhᵘ, nū̃ṭhᵘ; L. naṭṭhā; P. naṭṭhṇā 'to flee'; WPah. cur. naṭhā, (Joshi) naṭhṇu 'to flee'; A. nāṭh 'lost'; B. nāṭ(h) 'spoilt, corrupted', naṭhā 'to go sour (of milk)'; OAw. nāṭhi f. 'she was lost'; H. nāṭh m. 'destruction', nāṭhnā, nā̃ṭh° 'to be destroyed' (whence tr. 'to destroy' and intr. naṭhnā 'to be destroyed'); G. nāṭhũ 'fled'; M. nāṭ 'lost'; Si. naṭa 'destroyed'. — In some cases difficult, both phonet. and semant., to separate from *naṭṭha- s.v. *naṭṭa-. But < naṣṭá- prob. M. nāṭ 'bankrupt' ~ Pa. naṭṭhāyika-; and poss. H. naṭhiyā m. 'scoundrel' (cf. esp. OMarw. vinaṭhī f. 'wretch' < vínaṣṭa-); M. nāṭ(h)ā 'vile'; M. naṭhārā 'bad, useless', G. naṭhārũ 'rude, unbecoming'.
    Addenda: náśyati. 1. WPah.kṭg. náśṇõ 'to go, run away', J. naśṇu (rāmp. nā́ṇõ 'to go away' see †náśati).
    2. naṣṭá-: WPah.rāmp. (pret. of nā́ṇõ) naṭṭhɔ; — OP. nāṭhī, nāṭhiaṛā m. 'fleeting visitor'.

10948 lábhatē 'catches, takes' AitBr. (lábhēt AV., labhati MBh.) [~ rábhatē. — √labh]
    Some NIA. forms, esp.
